haiku-low.q1: The connection comes back, the app comes to the foreground, or 60 seconds pass while online.
haiku-low.q2: Upload first, then download. Download runs only after a successful upload step in the same run.
haiku-low.q3: The server detects it. It compares the change's base version with the note's current server version; a difference means conflict.
haiku-low.q4: Note N at version 6 with phone A's body A2, plus a new conflict note N2 titled 'N title (conflict)' holding body B at version 1.
haiku-low.q5: One change carrying the original base version and the latest body, since repeated edits update the same queued row.
haiku-low.q6: The server looks up (device id, change id) in applied_changes first. If found, it returns the stored result and writes nothing.
haiku-low.q7: On the phone, in sync_cursor, holding the last seq applied. It moves only in the same local transaction that applies a download page.
haiku-low.q8: The run ends and the cursor stays where it was. The whole page is fetched again at the next run.
haiku-low.q9: The conflict result tells the phone; its row is deleted, and N2 arrives via download. Local N keeps its body until a download with a higher version replaces it.
haiku-low.q10: When the server returns its result for it (accepted or conflict), the row is deleted. Rows with no result or a server error stay sending.
haiku-low.q11: The download replaces the local body and version even with a pending row. The row keeps its own body and base, later conflicts, and is saved as a conflict note.
haiku-low.q12: The sent row is never changed. The new edit becomes a separate queued row with base set to the last applied version; it uploads later and may conflict.

sonnet.q1: Connection coming back, app coming to the foreground, or 60 seconds passing while online. A trigger during a run does nothing (single-flight lock).
sonnet.q2: Upload first (batches of up to 100 while rows wait), then download (pages of up to 500 until a page has fewer than 500). Download runs only after a successful upload step.
sonnet.q3: The server. It compares the change's base version with the note's current server version under the note lock. If they differ, it is a conflict.
sonnet.q4: Note N at version 6 with the first phone's body (A2), plus a new conflict note N2 (title is N's title plus (conflict), body B, version 1). The change log has seq 101 for N and seq 102 for N2.
sonnet.q5: One change. The edits update the same queued outbox row, which keeps its change id and original base version and holds the latest full body.
sonnet.q6: The retry sends the same change id. The server looks up (device id, change id) in applied_changes before any base check or lock. If found, it returns the stored result and writes nothing.
sonnet.q7: In the phone's sync_cursor, which holds the last seq applied. It is updated only in the same local transaction that applies a download page.
sonnet.q8: The run ends and the cursor stays where it was. Nothing from the partial page is applied. The next run fetches the whole page again from the old cursor.
sonnet.q9: The conflict result tells the phone, and the phone deletes the row. It does not store N2's id and its local N keeps its body and version. A later download brings the server's N (higher version replaces body and version) and creates N2. The conflict result does not carry the server version.
sonnet.q10: When the phone applies an accepted or conflict result for it, and the row is deleted. Rows with no result or a server error stay (as sending, then sent) and are retried.
sonnet.q11: The download replaces the local body and version with the server's, even when a row is pending. The pending row keeps its own body and base and is not changed. Its later upload conflicts and its body is saved as a conflict note. The UI meanwhile shows the server's body. Whether the UI should keep showing the pending edit is undecided.
sonnet.q12: A new queued row is added, because a sent or sending change is never modified. Its base is the last version the phone applied. That is older than the in-flight change's result, so it will probably conflict and be saved as an extra conflict note. Nothing is lost.
